name: Baruch
overview: Baruch was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as the son of Col-hozeh. His mention in Nehemiah 11:5 places him among the post-exilic community, though no additional notes expand on his personal story or role. This brief record highlights his tribal affiliation and lineage within the restored Israelite community.
namesAndTitles: The name Baruch means 'be blessed,' reflecting a common Hebrew blessing name. It is a proper name and was not given directly by God, as noted in Nehemiah 11:5. This name suggests a positive and hopeful meaning consistent with the post-exilic period of restoration.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Baruch as the son of Col-hozeh and infers Maaseiah as his father, both referenced in Nehemiah 11:5. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented, limiting our understanding to these immediate connections.
scriptureSignificance: Baruch's significance lies in his inclusion among the returning exiles in the tribe of Judah, as identified in Nehemiah 11:5. His lineage as the son of Col-hozeh situates him within the community that resettled and rebuilt Jerusalem after the Babylonian captivity. Though not extensively detailed, Baruch represents the faithful remnant preserved by God's providence during this critical period of restoration.
